angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 874,077 km at 144.30 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.9298 +/- 0.0100 mas (same row, RUWE 0.92): 144.30 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.2564 +/- 0.0084 solar radii from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-68 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract): 874,077 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.057 +/- 0.022 solar masses from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-68 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5847 +/- 75 K from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-68 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-68 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-68.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.264, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
